extended_qna.question: If you had 30 seconds to describe your edge as a developer, what would you say?
extended_qna.answer: I bridge the gap between frontend user experience, robust backend APIs, and emerging AI/security tooling. Rather than just building static UI or writing raw scripts, I focus on end-to-end execution—from containerizing apps in Docker and hardening endpoints to shipping live platforms like Placement Pro and Pure Weaves that solve real operational friction.

extended_qna.question: How do you approach choosing the right tech stack for a project?
extended_qna.answer: I prioritize project requirements and maintainability over hype. For instance, when high-throughput API speed and auto-generated OpenAPI documentation were critical for the Placement Pro portal, I chose FastAPI. For lightweight, stateful local utilities, I use Electron.js or standard Python. I select relational engines like PostgreSQL or MySQL when data integrity is paramount, and NoSQL when schema flexibility drives speed.

extended_qna.question: Can you describe a challenging technical bug you encountered and resolved?
extended_qna.answer: While integrating real-time catalog ordering workflows for Pure Weaves, handling asynchronous session updates alongside WhatsApp checkout redirects caused payload mismatches. I debugged the event listeners and state management flow, restructured the backend validation handlers, and tested the request-response cycle locally before redeploying to Railway, eliminating edge-case drops.

extended_qna.question: How do you integrate security into your daily development workflow?
extended_qna.answer: Security is not an afterthought. I write input validation logic to mitigate injection and XSS vulnerabilities, implement sanitized SQL queries with parameterized statements, handle CORS headers properly, and practice environment isolation using Docker. My hands-on work with Kali Linux and network auditing tools gives me an offensive perspective to build better defensive code.

extended_qna.question: How do you practically integrate AI into software rather than using it as a buzzword?
extended_qna.answer: I integrate AI to solve specific workflow bottlenecks. That includes implementing computer vision pipelines with OpenCV and YOLOv8 for detection tasks, building RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) setups with vector embeddings for context-specific question answering, and automating recurring data ingestion workflows in Python.

extended_qna.question: How do you keep up with rapid changes in web frameworks and AI?
extended_qna.answer: I follow a build-to-learn methodology. Instead of only reading documentation, I build isolated proof-of-concept projects, test tools in sandbox environments, and earn structured certifications—having completed over 87 technical courses. I also track open-source repositories and document developer workflows daily.

extended_qna.question: Describe a time you collaborated under pressure during an event or deadline.
extended_qna.answer: During the setup for HACK4 SHIVAMOGGA, we needed an immediate, reliable registration portal and schedule system with rapid turnarounds. I took ownership of the landing page architecture and automated data sync into backend sheets under tight timelines, coordinating closely with faculty and student volunteers to ensure zero registration downtime.

extended_qna.question: What does clean code mean to you?
extended_qna.answer: Clean code means readability, predictable side effects, and clear separation of concerns. I ensure variable and function names convey intent, adhere to modular folder structures in frontend and backend code, write descriptive commit messages, and document API contracts clearly so any teammate can onboard without friction.

extended_qna.question: How do you handle a project requirement that is vague or incomplete?
extended_qna.answer: I clarify goals by building a quick minimal viable prototype (MVP) to anchor discussions. For example, when building GrabNotes, initial requirements for note categorization were fluid; I drafted a functional UI prototype with basic CRUD operations, gathered direct student feedback on navigation friction, and iterated based on real usage patterns.

extended_qna.question: What drives you to build software every day?
extended_qna.answer: I enjoy turning abstract logic into tools people actually use. Seeing a system go from an empty code editor to a containerized, live deployment handling real user requests—like students checking placement opportunities or customers browsing an artisan catalog—is what keeps me building every day.

extended_qna.question: Why should our company hire you over other candidates?
extended_qna.answer: I bring a balance of full-stack development speed, security-first thinking, and genuine shipping discipline. While many students keep projects local, I have deployed 8+ live platforms, delivered production software like Placement Pro and Pure Weaves, earned 87+ technical certifications, and gained hands-on industry experience at Milano Infotech. I ramp up quickly and contribute directly from day one.

extended_qna.question: How do you handle receiving critical feedback or code review rejections?
extended_qna.answer: I view code reviews as an engineering audit, not a personal critique. If a senior developer flags an unoptimized database query or redundant state handler, I ask clarifying questions to understand the architectural reason, benchmark the improvement, refactor the code, and document the standard to avoid repeating the mistake.

extended_qna.question: Do you work better independently or within a team?
extended_qna.answer: I operate comfortably in both modes. For deep technical tasks like debugging an API router, configuring Dockerfiles, or writing automation scripts, I work with strong independent focus. When it comes to product roadmaps, cross-functional sprints, or event operations like Hack4 Shivamogga, I actively collaborate, communicate blockers early, and support teammates to hit deadlines.

extended_qna.question: Tell me about a time something went wrong with a deployment or project. What did you learn?
extended_qna.answer: During an early deployment of a web application, an unhandled environment variable caused database connections to fail on the cloud server. Rather than panicking, I inspected runtime logs, identified the missing credential mapping, patched the config, and added structured `.env.example` templates and health-check endpoints. It taught me the necessity of robust deployment checklists.

extended_qna.question: How do you prioritize your workload when juggling multiple urgent tasks?
extended_qna.answer: I use an impact-versus-urgency matrix to sequence my work. I break large deliverables into discrete 30-to-60-minute development blocks, tackle core blockers first, automate repetitive steps with Python, and communicate proactively with stakeholders if scope trade-offs are required to safeguard product quality and ship on time.

extended_qna.question: How do you approach learning a programming language or framework you haven't used before?
extended_qna.answer: I deconstruct new technologies by mapping them to concepts I already master. When picking up a new framework, I immediately build a basic CRUD application to understand its routing, state management, and database connectivity. Hands-on implementation combined with official documentation gets me productive within days.

extended_qna.question: Tell me about an instance where you took initiative without being asked.
extended_qna.answer: Seeing students struggle with disorganized academic materials, I independently initiated and designed GrabNotes to centralize and index study resources. Similarly, for Hack4 Shivamogga, I stepped up to build the public registration and schedule landing page to ensure participants had a smooth, zero-latency sign-up experience.

extended_qna.question: How do you handle ethical dilemmas in software, such as security vulnerabilities or data privacy?
extended_qna.answer: I prioritize user trust and systemic security over quick fixes. If I identify a security flaw or an exposed endpoint, I follow responsible disclosure principles immediately: isolate the risk, document the vulnerability vector, notify the team lead, and assist in implementing secure patches before code reaches production.
